# nanobot
## HarnessBench adapter
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from harnessbench.adapters.base import BaseAdapter
from harnessbench.models import AdapterRunContext, AdapterRunResult
from harnessbench.usage_proxy import register_routes


def _project_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _resolve_project_path(raw: str | Path) -> Path:
    p = Path(os.path.expanduser(str(raw)))
    if not p.is_absolute():
        p = _project_root() / p
    return p.resolve()


def _merge_user_config(
    user_config: Path,
    workspace: Path,
    out_path: Path,
    proxy_base_url: str = "",
    proxy_routes_file: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    data = json.loads(user_config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data.setdefault("agents", {}).setdefault("defaults", {})["workspace"] = str(workspace)
    if proxy_base_url and proxy_routes_file is not None:
        routes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        providers = data.get("providers") or {}
        if isinstance(providers, dict):
            for provider_name, provider_cfg in providers.items():
                if not isinstance(provider_cfg, dict):
                    continue
                upstream = str(provider_cfg.get("apiBase") or "").strip()
                if not upstream:
                    continue
                prefix = f"/nanobot/{provider_name}"
                routes[prefix] = {
                    "framework": "nanobot",
                    "provider": str(provider_name),
                    "upstream": upstream,
                }
                provider_cfg["apiBase"] = f"{proxy_base_url}{prefix}"
        if routes:
            register_routes(proxy_routes_file, routes)
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")


class NanoBotAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    name = "nanobot"

    def run(self, ctx: AdapterRunContext) -> AdapterRunResult:
        command = str(ctx.model_config.get("command") or "nanobot")
        user_config_raw = str(ctx.model_config.get("user_config") or "config/nanobot.json")
        user_config = _resolve_project_path(user_config_raw)
        if not user_config.is_file():
            return AdapterRunResult(ok=False, stderr=f"missing NanoBot source config: {user_config}")

        isolated_home = ctx.sandbox
        nanobot_home = isolated_home / ".nanobot"
        nanobot_home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        nanobot_workspace = nanobot_home / "workspace"
        nanobot_workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        sandbox_user_config = nanobot_home / "nanobot_src.json"
        shutil.copy2(user_config, sandbox_user_config)
        merged_cfg = nanobot_home / "nanobot.json"
        _merge_user_config(
            sandbox_user_config,
            nanobot_workspace,
            merged_cfg,
            proxy_base_url=str(ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_URL") or ""),
            proxy_routes_file=Path(ctx.env["HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES"]) if ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES") else None,
        )

        cmd = [
            command,
            "agent",
            "--message",
            ctx.prompt,
            "--session",
            ctx.session_id,
            "--workspace",
            str(nanobot_workspace),
            "--config",
            str(merged_cfg),
        ]
        if bool(ctx.model_config.get("no_markdown")):
            cmd.append("--no-markdown")
        if bool(ctx.model_config.get("logs")):
            cmd.append("--logs")
        else:
            cmd.append("--no-logs")

        env = os.environ.copy()
        env.update(ctx.env)
        env["HOME"] = str(isolated_home)
        env["NANOBOT_HOME"] = str(nanobot_home)
        env["NANOBOT_WORKSPACE"] = str(nanobot_workspace)
        env["WORKSPACE"] = str(ctx.workspace)
        completed = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            cwd=str(ctx.sandbox),
            text=True,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=ctx.timeout_sec,
            env=env,
            check=False,
        )
        return AdapterRunResult(
            ok=completed.returncode == 0,
            command=cmd,
            stdout=completed.stdout,
            stderr=completed.stderr,
            metadata={
                "returncode": completed.returncode,
                "nanobot_config_path": str(merged_cfg),
                "source_user_config_path": str(user_config),
                "sandbox_user_config_path": str(sandbox_user_config),
                "isolated_home": str(isolated_home),
                "nanobot_home": str(nanobot_home),
                "nanobot_workspace": str(nanobot_workspace),
                "workspace": str(ctx.workspace),
            },
        )

# nanobot

🐈 **nanobot** is an ultra-lightweight, open-source, self-hosted personal AI agent framework written in Python. It runs in a WebUI, terminal, or chat apps and combines tools, long-term memory, MCP integrations, model routing, multi-agent delegation, scheduled automation, and an OpenAI-compatible API in a small, readable core.

## Start Here

| You want to... | Go to |
|---|---|
| Install nanobot with no terminal/config background | [Start Without Technical Background](./docs/start-without-technical-background.md) |
| Install quickly and get one CLI reply | [Install](#-install) and [Quick Start](#-quick-start) |
| Open the bundled browser UI | [WebUI](#-webui) |
| Connect Telegram, Discord, WeChat, Slack, Email, Mattermost, Linear, or another channel | [Chat Apps](./docs/chat-apps.md) |
| Configure providers, fallback models, Langfuse, MCP, web tools, or security | [Docs](./docs/README.md) and [Configuration](./docs/configuration.md) |
| Understand or extend the internals | [Architecture](./docs/architecture.md) and [Development](./docs/development.md) |
| Deploy to the cloud or keep nanobot running as a service | [Deployment](./docs/deployment.md) |

## What can nanobot do?

nanobot is a self-hosted personal AI agent runtime. It can:

- run in a browser WebUI or terminal
- connect to Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, Email, Mattermost, Linear, and other channels
- use tools such as files, shell, web search, web fetch, MCP, cron, image generation, and subagents
- keep session history and long-term memory through Dream
- run long-horizon goals and scheduled automations
- expose a Python SDK and OpenAI-compatible API for integrations
- deploy as a long-running local or server-side agent gateway

## 💡 Why nanobot

- **Persistent workflows**: goals, memory, tools, and chat context survive long-running work.
- **Chat-native reach**: WebUI, API, Telegram, Feishu, Slack, Discord, Teams, email, Mattermost, and Linear.
- **Model freedom**: OpenAI-compatible APIs, local LLMs, image generation, search, and fallbacks.
- **Small core**: readable internals with MCP, memory, deployment, and automation built in.
- **Own your stack**: inspect, customize, self-host, and extend without a giant platform.

## 📦 Install

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If you want the newest features and experiments, install from source.
>
> If you want the most stable day-to-day experience, install from PyPI or with `uv`.

Pick **one** install method:

| Track | Install with | Update with | What runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stable | installer, `uv`, or pip | the same package tool | one released Python/WebUI/TUI version |
| Current source | editable Git checkout | `git pull --ff-only` + editable dependency sync | Python, WebUI, and TUI from that checkout |

Prerequisites: Python 3.11 or newer. Git and [Bun](https://bun.sh/) are only needed for a source install. Published packages include the WebUI, and supported platform wheels also include the native TUI. A source-distribution install can fetch a checksummed, version-matched TUI archive—with its licenses, notices, corresponding application source, source offer, and relinking instructions—on first use.

If terminals, API keys, or config files are new to you, use the guided zero-background walkthrough in [Start Without Technical Background](./docs/start-without-technical-background.md) instead of this compact README path.

**One-command setup**

macOS / Linux:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

The default command installs or upgrades `nanobot-ai` from PyPI. On a fresh local desktop, it then starts `nanobot webui` so you can configure the first provider and model in **Settings → Models**. SSH, headless, existing-config, and older-release paths keep the terminal setup wizard. The installer avoids system-wide pip installs by using an active virtual environment, `uv`, `pipx`, or a managed venv under `~/.nanobot/venv`. It also prints the exact command it used to run nanobot; reuse that full command below if `nanobot` is not on `PATH`.

To preview the plan without changing your environment, pass `--dry-run`.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --dry-run
```

```powershell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1))) --dry-run
```

If you prefer to inspect the script first, open [`scripts/install.sh`](./scripts/install.sh) or [`scripts/install.ps1`](./scripts/install.ps1).

**Install with `uv`**

```bash
uv tool install nanobot-ai
```

**Install from PyPI with pip**

```bash
python -m pip install nanobot-ai
```

If pip reports `externally-managed-environment` on macOS or Linux, use the one-command installer, `uv tool install nanobot-ai`, `pipx install nanobot-ai`, or install inside a virtual environment.

Platform wheels include both the WebUI and the native terminal UI: macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon
and Intel), glibc 2.17+ Linux (ARM64 and x64), and Windows x64. The x64 runtime requires SSE4.2.
Pip selects the matching wheel; opening the TUI does not need a separate GitHub download or Bun
installation. A source-distribution install on a supported target can use the matching checksummed
GitHub release archive. On other platforms, use `nanobot --classic` or the WebUI.

**Install from source**

Clone the repository and install it in editable mode. Bun is required because the source
checkout runs the matching TUI directly instead of downloading an older release binary.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot.git
cd nanobot
python -m venv .venv
```

Activate it with `source .venv/bin/activate` on macOS/Linux or
`.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in Windows PowerShell, then run:

```bash
python -m pip install -e .
```

After that, the normal commands are identical to a stable install. `nanobot` runs the TUI
from this checkout, and `nanobot webui` rebuilds stale frontend assets automatically. A later
`git pull --ff-only` updates the Python, TUI, and WebUI source together; rerun
`python -m pip install -e .` when Python dependencies change. Contributors should also read
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

Verify the install:

```bash
nanobot --version
```

If `nanobot` is not on `PATH`, invoke it through the method that installed it: reuse the recommended installer's command, use `uv tool run --from nanobot-ai nanobot ...` or `pipx run --spec nanobot-ai nanobot ...`, or use the Python executable from the environment where pip installed the package.

## 🚀 Quick Start

**Open nanobot in your browser**

```bash
nanobot webui
```

This is the recommended first run. The launcher creates the config and workspace when needed, safely enables the local WebSocket channel after confirmation, starts or joins the shared local gateway, and opens [`http://127.0.0.1:8765`](http://127.0.0.1:8765). A fresh install can open before a model is configured, so setup continues in the browser instead of beginning in a JSON file. The first-run WebUI binds to localhost by default and is not exposed to your LAN.

**Your first three steps**

1. Open **Settings → Models** and choose a provider, credential, and model.
2. Start a new topic and send `Hello!` to verify the connection.
3. Before project work, choose the intended workspace and access mode from the composer.

Any normal reply means the provider, model, workspace, and browser gateway are working together.

**Keep nanobot running after you close the terminal**

```bash
nanobot gateway --background
```

This is the only command that promotes the shared gateway to persistent background mode. It leaves channels and automations running after every local TUI and WebUI launcher exits. Complete first-time model setup with `nanobot webui` before switching to background mode; open the same localhost WebUI again afterward.

```bash
nanobot gateway status
nanobot gateway logs
nanobot gateway restart
nanobot gateway stop
```

**Prefer a gateway-first workflow?**

```bash
nanobot gateway
```

This skips WebUI setup and browser opening, then runs the same complete gateway in the current terminal. It is the familiar entry point if you are coming from OpenClaw or already operate agents as long-lived services. The WebUI remains available when its channel is configured; open it manually when needed.

Use `nanobot gateway --background` for the same direct entry point without keeping the terminal attached. For automatic startup and supervision by the operating system, see [Deployment](./docs/deployment.md).

**Prefer to work entirely in the terminal?**

```bash
nanobot
```

This opens the native terminal client with the launch directory as its workspace. It shares saved conversations and the local gateway with the WebUI. The explicit `nanobot agent` form remains available for compatibility.

- Type `/` to discover commands, `/sessions` to switch conversations, or `@` to mention an app, MCP server, or saved session.
- Paste clipboard images with `Ctrl+V` or `Alt+V`, and use `$` to complete skill references.
- Use `/diff` to inspect file changes, `/context` to inspect session context, or `/branch` to continue from a completed reply in a new session.
- Press `Enter` to send. While nanobot is working, `Enter` sends now and `Tab` sends after the current response. Press `Shift+Enter` to add a newline (`Ctrl+J` works in terminals that cannot distinguish modified Enter keys).
- Use `/detach` to leave the current task running, or start with `nanobot gateway --background` when nanobot should stay online after all local clients exit.

Each launch starts a new session by default. Use `--session` to resume one and `--workspace` to choose another workspace. See the [CLI reference](./docs/cli-reference.md#agent-cli) for session branching, diffs, history, shortcuts, gateway lifecycle, and compatibility options.

For one request and an immediate exit, use:

```bash
nanobot -m "Hello!"
```

The one-shot form is useful for a quick provider check, shell scripts, and local automation. If you have not configured a model yet, run `nanobot webui` and open **Settings → Models** first.

Need manual JSON, another device on your LAN, or help with provider/model matching? Continue with [Install and Quick Start](./docs/quick-start.md), [WebUI](./docs/webui.md), or [Troubleshooting](./docs/troubleshooting.md).

If nanobot worked for you, a star on GitHub is the simplest way to support the project.

- Want a pasteable provider setup? See [Provider Cookbook](./docs/provider-cookbook.md)
- Want to understand provider/model matching? See [Providers and Models](./docs/providers.md)
- Want web search, MCP, security settings, or more config options? See [Configuration](./docs/configuration.md)
- Want to run locally? See [Ollama](./docs/providers.md#ollama), [vLLM or another local OpenAI-compatible server](./docs/providers.md#vllm-or-other-local-openai-compatible-server), and the full [provider reference](./docs/configuration.md#providers).
- Want to run nanobot in chat apps like Telegram, Discord, WeChat or Feishu? See [Chat Apps](./docs/chat-apps.md)
- Want Docker or Linux service deployment? See [Deployment](./docs/deployment.md)

<a id="deploy-to-render"></a>

## ☁️ Deploy

**Render — one click**

Deploy nanobot's gateway and bundled WebUI from the repository's ready-to-use Blueprint:

[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot)

Render will ask for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and a private `NANOBOT_WEB_TOKEN`, then provision persistent storage for sessions, memory, and WebUI history. Persistent disks require a paid Render service.

**Self-host**

Prefer your own infrastructure? Follow the [deployment guide](./docs/deployment.md) for Docker, Docker Compose, Linux services, and macOS LaunchAgent setup.

## 🌐 WebUI

The WebUI ships **inside the published wheel** with no separate frontend build. It is the browser workbench for persistent topics, temporary chats, visible agent activity, workspace controls, Apps, Skills, Automations, and settings. Start it with `nanobot webui`.

The screenshots below use example conversations, illustrative token counts, and paused schedules.

<p align="center">
  <a href="./images/nanobot_webui-source.png">
    <img src="./images/nanobot_webui.png" alt="nanobot WebUI new-topic screen with the hero composer, workspace access, project, and model controls" width="900">
  </a>
</p>

Use it to:

- keep separate topics for different tasks and projects;
- use temporary chats when a conversation should not be saved to history or memory;
- inspect reasoning, tool calls, file edits, diffs, command output, and generated artifacts;
- switch models and workspaces without leaving the conversation;
- configure providers and chat channels, connect Apps, discover Skills, and manage Automations from one place.

### Keep related work side by side

Group up to four conversations and arrange them in columns, rows, a grid, or a main pane with supporting panes. Each topic keeps its own history. Select another topic from the `@` menu, or drag it into the composer, to let the agent read its context and coordinate work across sessions.

<p align="center">
  <img src="./images/nanobot-workbench.png" alt="Three conversations in one workbench: a release plan beside quick-start work and documentation review" width="900">
</p>

Choose a project, access mode, and model for each task. Attach documents or images, then send follow-ups immediately or queue them for the next response. [Explore topics and panes →](./docs/webui.md#conversation-groups-and-panes)

### Inspect the work and its context

Expand agent activity to see reasoning, tool calls, and file changes. Switch **Settings → Appearance → File edit display** to **Diff** for inline patches. The composer's context indicator shows the current context size, input tokens by round, and cache reuse when the provider reports it.

<p align="center">
  <img src="./images/nanobot-context.png" alt="An expanded file-edit diff above the context usage chart, with input tokens and cache reuse shown across four rounds" width="900">
</p>

Context compaction also appears in the conversation timeline. [Explore activity and context →](./docs/webui.md#activity-and-context-usage)

### Bring your tools into the conversation

Use Apps to connect MCP servers, enable Agent Plugins, and manage local CLI App adapters. Add a preset or a custom server, then attach an available tool with `@`. Skills provide reusable instructions; Settings holds model, voice, image, web, and chat-channel setup.

<p align="center">
  <img src="./images/nanobot-apps.png" alt="The Apps MCP catalog with integration presets and controls to add or import a custom MCP server" width="900">
</p>

[Explore Apps →](./docs/webui.md#apps) · [Discover Skills →](./docs/webui.md#skills) · [Connect chat apps →](./docs/chat-apps.md)

### Let recurring work run on a schedule

Ask for an automation from the topic that should receive its results. Use **Tasks** to review and manage schedules, or **Calendar** to scan completed and upcoming runs by date. Local triggers let a script start a saved task on demand.

<p align="center">
  <img src="./images/nanobot-automations.png" alt="The Automations calendar with completed and upcoming recurring tasks arranged by date" width="900">
</p>

Keep the gateway running for scheduled delivery. [Explore Automations →](./docs/automations.md)

For a conversation that should stay out of saved topic history and long-term memory, use [Temporary chat](./docs/webui.md#temporary-chats) from the header. Temporary chats end when the connection closes and use the default workspace in Restricted mode.

See the [WebUI guide](./docs/webui.md) for LAN access, background operation, workspace controls, and the full feature tour. Working on the frontend itself? Use [`webui/README.md`](./webui/README.md).

## Architecture

<p align="center">
  <img src="images/nanobot_arch.png" alt="nanobot architecture" width="800">
</p>

🐈 nanobot stays lightweight by centering everything around a small agent loop: messages come in from chat apps, the LLM decides when tools are needed, and memory or skills are pulled in only as context instead of becoming a heavy orchestration layer. That keeps the core path readable and easy to extend, while still letting you add channels, tools, memory, and deployment options without turning the system into a monolith.

## Releases

**Latest release: [v0.3.5](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/releases/tag/v0.3.5)**

v0.3.5 brings the workbench to the terminal and makes conversations easier to continue across the browser, terminal, and chat apps.

- Use the native terminal workbench with the same gateway and saved conversations as the WebUI.
- Arrange up to four browser conversations side by side, mention saved sessions, or open a temporary chat.
- Inspect per-round context usage and compaction progress, with more durable history and recovery.
- Discover Skills, connect Apps, and manage scheduled work through expanded WebUI flows.

[Read the v0.3.5 release notes and upgrade notes](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/releases/tag/v0.3.5)

## Recent Updates

- **2026-09-19** 🔎 Searchable provider setup, consistent provider identities, and smoother Linear onboarding.
- **2026-09-18** ♻️ Clearer recovery for interrupted work and Discord reply-context support.
- **2026-09-16** 📦 Platform wheels bundle the version-matched native terminal UI.
- **2026-09-15** 🚀 Released [v0.3.5](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/releases/tag/v0.3.5) with a shared terminal workbench, multi-pane WebUI, and visible context continuity.
- **2026-09-07** 🔌 WeCom media uploads use the SDK API, and CI skips unrelated jobs.

For earlier updates, see the [release archive](./docs/release-archive.md) or [GitHub releases](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/releases).

## 🤝 Contribute

Use nanobot for a real task, report what broke, and then pick a focused improvement.

- Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow.
- Browse [open issues](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues) for problems to investigate.
- Open a [pull request](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pulls) for a focused fix or integration.

--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-54-After Desktop is selected, a disconnect or incompatible reply ends that invocation
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-55-with an error; it never silently switches to Python or launches a replacement.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:56:On macOS, browser URLs are delivered through native Launch Services rather than
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-57-command-line arguments. A failed native handoff does not fall back to `open` or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:58:a `BROWSER` command, keeping bootstrap credentials out of launcher arguments.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-59-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:60:On Windows, the shared browser launcher uses a private HTML redirect rather than
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:61:passing a credential-bearing URL to a browser command. A short-lived, windowless
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-62-Python helper receives the URL over an anonymous pipe, opens the redirect through
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-63-the system's HTTP association, and attempts file cleanup after two minutes. The calling
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-64-CLI can exit immediately after the launch acknowledgement; this helper does not
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:65:start, stop, or keep a gateway alive. It does not honor `BROWSER` overrides.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-66-Redirects are stored in the current user's Windows Local AppData known folder,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:67:under `NanobotBrowserHandoff-v1`, with an explicit current-user-only protected ACL.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-68-An ACL-enforcing local filesystem and a non-reparse storage path are required;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:69:unsafe existing storage or failed browser handoff fails without raw-URL fallback.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-70-Abnormal termination can leave a private redirect behind. Later invocations retry
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-71-cleanup of verified redirect files older than ten minutes, excluding active files;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-72-cleanup is not a guarantee of physical erasure or secrecy from same-user programs
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:73:or administrators. No Python/Desktop settings, credentials, or history are imported
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-74-between installations.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-75-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-76-Any explicit subcommand or option—including `nanobot agent`,

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-78-and gateway lifecycle commands—keeps its existing Python meaning and never opens
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-79-the Desktop picker. Target choices are not remembered, and Desktop settings are

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:160:Inside the native TUI, `/sessions` switches saved conversations, `/new-chat` starts another saved
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:161:conversation, and `/context` explains the compacted summary and raw session suffix available to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-162-the next agent turn. `/branch` forks a saved conversation from a completed reply, and `/diff`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:163:opens the latest turn's file changes as a full-screen unified diff.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-164-`PageUp` loads older transcript pages when you reach the top. By default, each launch starts a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:165:new session using the launch directory as its workspace. `--session` selects a specific existing
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:166:session, and `--workspace` overrides the launch directory. When the TUI exits, it prints a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:167:ready-to-run `nanobot agent --session ...` command for the current session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-168-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:169:## Session Storage and Rollback
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-170-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:171:Session JSONL files live under `<config-dir>/sessions/<workspace-id>/`, outside the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:172:agent-readable workspace. On the first upgraded start, nanobot safely migrates existing
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:173:`<workspace>/sessions/*.jsonl` files after verifying an atomic copy. Stop every old nanobot
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:174:process that uses the workspace before upgrading; old and new binaries must not write the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:175:same session concurrently.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-176-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:177:To prepare a downgrade, stop nanobot and copy the current sessions back to the path understood
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-178-by older releases:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-179-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:180:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:181:nanobot sessions restore-workspace --config ./bot-a/config.json --workspace ./bot-a/workspace
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-182-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-183-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-184-The command never deletes the external store and refuses to overwrite a different existing
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:185:workspace file. Back up both the config directory and workspace before changing versions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-186-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:187:Interactive mode uses nanobot's native TypeScript terminal UI. It talks to the same local gateway as the WebUI, so streaming, tool progress, and WebSocket sessions share one protocol instead of maintaining a second agent loop. If no gateway is running, either client starts it on demand. The TUI paints immediately while the local gateway starts, then obtains fresh bootstrap credentials and connects in the background. Exiting one TUI or WebUI launcher releases only that client; the last interactive launcher stops the on-demand gateway. A small gateway watchdog also reclaims an on-demand process if its last client crashes. `/detach` promotes the shared gateway to persistent background mode before closing the TUI, so active agent work continues without a connected client. An explicit `nanobot gateway --background` starts or promotes the gateway the same way before opening a client. `nanobot gateway restart` restarts a detached gateway without changing that lifetime; restart an attached foreground gateway in its owning terminal. `nanobot gateway stop` ends either mode.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-188-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:189:The default `--theme auto` mode paints first with the terminal's default background, probes the real foreground and background colors asynchronously, and follows supported live appearance changes. Use `--theme light` or `--theme dark` when a terminal or multiplexer does not report its colors reliably. The model preset and workspace access labels above the composer can be clicked to open their selectors; arrow keys, `Enter`, and `Esc` provide the same controls without a mouse. Access changes still pass through the gateway's local-trust and active-turn policy checks.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-190-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:191:`Enter` sends the current message. While nanobot is working, `Enter` sends immediately, `Tab` waits until the current response is finished, and `Option+Up` on macOS (`Alt+Up` on Windows/Linux) returns the latest waiting message to the composer. Press `Shift+Enter` to add a newline; `Ctrl+J` is the universal fallback when a terminal cannot distinguish modified Enter keys. `Alt+Enter` and `Ctrl+Enter` are also accepted when distinguishable. Use `Up`/`Down` at the composer edge to recall prompts from the current saved session. Large pastes appear as a compact placeholder in the composer but are sent unchanged. Type `/` to discover nanobot commands and terminal navigation in one palette, or type `@` to complete installed apps, configured MCP servers, and saved sessions. Use the arrow keys to choose an item and `Tab` to complete it. `/sessions` opens a searchable conversation picker, `/new-chat` preserves the current conversation and starts another one, and `/branch` forks from a completed reply. `/diff` opens a read-only unified diff for the newest turn; use `Left`/`Right` to switch edits and `Esc` to close it. The core `/new` command retains its cross-channel behavior and resets the current chat. `Ctrl+C` copies a selection, stops a running turn, clears a non-empty composer, or exits when idle. Use `PageUp`/`PageDown` to scroll, `Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End` to jump to the transcript edges, and `Ctrl+O` to expand or collapse long tool traces. When you leave the bottom, the TUI shows a scrollbar and a `Ctrl+End` hint until you return. The footer reports provider token/cache usage when available. Selections copy through OSC 52 when the terminal supports it. The transcript reflows when the terminal is resized, and exiting restores the previous screen.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-192-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-193-Platform wheels bundle the matching native terminal executable for macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon and Intel), glibc 2.17+ Linux (x64 and ARM64), and Windows x64. The x64 runtime requires SSE4.2. Its licenses, third-party notices, source offer, relinking instructions, and corresponding TUI source are installed alongside it in `nanobot/tui/bin/`. The launcher uses this bundled executable without downloading from GitHub or requiring Bun.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-197-Non-interactive input/output, `--logs`, and `--no-markdown` automatically retain the classic prompt so existing scripts and diagnostic workflows do not acquire terminal control sequences or silently ignore their options.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-198-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:199:Interactive mode exits with `exit`, `quit`, `/exit`, `/quit`, `:q`, or `Ctrl+D`. Use `/detach` instead to close the TUI without stopping the shared gateway or its active agent work. The restored terminal prints a copyable stop command with the same `--config` and explicit `--workspace` selectors.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-222-## Gateway
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-223-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:224:`nanobot gateway` starts enabled chat channels, WebUI/WebSocket when configured, cron-backed system jobs, Dream, heartbeat, and the health endpoint. Most local browser users should start with `nanobot webui`; use `gateway` directly for service management, chat app operation, and advanced deployment. By default it runs in the foreground, which keeps existing scripts and terminal workflows unchanged. Use `--background` when you want a local macOS, Linux, or Windows process that you can manage from the CLI.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-225-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:231:| `nanobot gateway --workspace <path>` | Override workspace |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-266-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-267-`nanobot trigger` delivers one local message to a trigger that was created from
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:268:a chat/session with `/trigger <name>`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-269-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:270:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-271-nanobot trigger trg_8K4P2Q9X "Review PR #4502"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-272-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-273-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-274-Keep `nanobot gateway` running so the message can be delivered to the linked
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:275:chat/session. The message is recorded as an automation turn in that session,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-276-not as a normal chat message typed by the user.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-277-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:278:The command writes to a workspace-local durable queue. If `nanobot gateway` is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:279:not running yet, the message waits in that workspace. If the target session is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:280:already running a turn, the trigger waits for that session to become idle. If the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-281-gateway exits after claiming a delivery but before the linked turn completes,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-282-the next gateway start requeues that delivery. The queue is at-least-once, not
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-284-process. If the agent receives the delivery and the turn fails, the delivery is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-285-marked failed instead of retried indefinitely. Each delivery also writes an
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:286:audit record under `<workspace>/triggers/runs`. Run one gateway consumer per
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:287:workspace; this local queue is not a distributed multi-consumer queue.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-288-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-289-Use stdin when another local process generates the message:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-290-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md:291:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-292-generate-report | nanobot trigger trg_8K4P2Q9X
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/cli-reference.md-293-```

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/openai-compatible-agent-api.md-32-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:1:# How to Improve Ollama Tool-Calling Prompt Cache Reuse in nanobot
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:3:Some Ollama model templates move or remove tool definitions as a conversation
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:4:switches between user, assistant, and tool messages. nanobot can send a correct
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-5-append-only chat request while the model template still renders a different token
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-6-prefix. On slower local hardware, re-evaluating that prefix can add tens of seconds
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:7:to an otherwise simple tool-using turn.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-8-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-9-This guide shows how to diagnose that specific pattern and create a derived
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:10:`llama3.1:8b` tag with a prefix-stable tool template. It does not modify nanobot or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-11-overwrite the original Ollama model.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-12-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-22-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-23-- direct Ollama responses are reasonably fast;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:24:- nanobot becomes slow after the model calls a tool;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:25:- Ollama logs show a long main prompt, a much shorter tool follow-up, and low
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-26-  initial cache reuse on the next main prompt;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:27:- the model is `llama3.1:8b` with a template that renders concrete tools only for
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-28-  the final user message.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-29-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-30-Do not apply this template to another model family without checking that model's
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:31:tool-call format first.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-32-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-33-## Diagnose the rendered prompt
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-38-**macOS or Linux**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-39-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:40:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:41:OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384 \
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-42-OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 \
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-43-OLLAMA_DEBUG=1 \
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-45-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-46-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:47:**Windows PowerShell**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-48-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:49:```powershell
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:50:$env:OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH = "16384"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-51-$env:OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL = "1"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-52-$env:OLLAMA_DEBUG = "1"
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-54-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-55-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:56:In another terminal, use a fresh session and explicitly request a tool so both
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-57-turns exercise the agent loop:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-58-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:59:```bash

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-87-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:88:The tested `llama3.1:8b` template conditionally expands the tool definitions inside
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-89-a user message:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-90-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-91-```gotemplate

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-96-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:97:The first request ends with a user message, so the tools are rendered there. After
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:98:nanobot appends an assistant tool call and its result, that user message is no
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:99:longer last, so the same API request history renders without the concrete tool
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:100:block. On the next user turn, the tools reappear at a new position.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-101-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-102-This is a model-template behavior. At the API boundary, nanobot continues to append
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:103:the assistant tool call and tool result and sends the same tool definitions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-104-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-224-## Limitations
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-225-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:226:- The template above is specific to the tested `llama3.1:8b` tool-call format.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-227-- Ollama or the model publisher may update the stock template in a later release.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:228:- Validate multiple tool calls, tool errors, parallel calls, and long conversations
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-229-  before using a custom template for unattended workloads.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md:230:- A higher cache ratio reduces prompt evaluation, but model generation, tool
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-231-  execution, process startup, and storage can still dominate end-to-end latency.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-ollama-prompt-cache.md-232-- Multiple Ollama slots change cache scheduling and may produce different results.
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:33:    "restrictToWorkspace": true,

--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-41-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-42-`bwrap` is Linux-only and requires bubblewrap. On macOS or Windows, keep
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:43:`restrictToWorkspace` enabled and review shell access carefully.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-44-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-45-## Production notes
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-47-- Use environment variables for provider keys, bot tokens, and mailbox
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-48-  passwords.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:49:- Keep one workspace per trust boundary.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-50-- Prefer pairing for DM-capable chat apps, use narrow `allowFrom` lists only
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-51-  when static allowlists are intentional, and keep group policy mention-only at
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-56-## Security notes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-57-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:58:- `restrictToWorkspace` is an application-level guard, not an OS sandbox.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:59:- `tools.exec.enable: false` removes shell execution entirely.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-60-- HTTP web fetch and HTTP MCP use SSRF protections by default.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:61:- Adding broad `tools.ssrfWhitelist` ranges increases exposure.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-62-- `allowFrom: ["*"]` bypasses pairing and means anyone who can reach that
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-63-  channel can talk to the bot.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-65-## Troubleshooting
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-66-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:67:- If a needed file cannot be read, confirm the active workspace path.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:68:- If a shell command fails under `bwrap`, check whether the command needs files
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-69-  outside the sandbox.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md:70:- If local HTTP tools are blocked, review the SSRF whitelist and use a narrow
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-71-  CIDR.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/secure-local-ai-agent.md-72-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/wechat-ai-agent.md-91-- If a first private message returns a pairing code, that is expected. Approve
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/wechat-ai-agent.md:92:  the code before testing normal agent replies.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/wechat-ai-agent.md-93-- If messages are denied without a pairing code, check gateway logs for whether
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/wechat-ai-agent.md:94:  WeChat provided the context token required for nanobot to reply.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/wechat-ai-agent.md-96-  the upstream service.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-48-    }
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-66-- In the WebUI, a reply produced by a named fallback preset shows its provider
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-67-  logo and preset name next to the reply timestamp. Hover, focus, or click the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md:68:  badge for an explanation. The composer still shows your selected preset;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-69-  primary replies have no fallback badge. Saved replies retain the name used
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-70-  for that invocation, even after a preset is renamed or deleted. Older replies
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-71-  without recorded attribution and unnamed inline fallback objects are not labeled.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md:72:- Keep fallback context windows realistic; smaller fallback windows constrain
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md:73:  how much context can fit.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-74-- Put cheaper or faster fallbacks before expensive ones when acceptable.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-75-- Use `/model <preset>` for runtime switching without editing config.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-89-  `modelPresets`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md-90-- If output is truncated after fallback, review `maxTokens` and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md:91:  `contextWindowTokens`.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:1:# How to Configure MCP Tools in nanobot
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:3:This guide adds an MCP server to nanobot so the agent can use external tools
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:4:through the Model Context Protocol.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-5-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-6-## What you will build
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-8-- a working nanobot agent
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-9-- one MCP integration configured through Apps or `~/.nanobot/config.json`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:10:- a restricted set of MCP tools exposed to the model
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-11-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-12-## When to use this
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-13-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-14-Use MCP when the capability you need already exists as an MCP server, or when
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:15:you want external tools to be managed outside nanobot core.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-16-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-17-## Install
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-18-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:19:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-20-python -m pip install nanobot-ai
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-21-nanobot onboard --wizard
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-34-   For a custom OAuth server, choose **OAuth** under **Authentication**, save it,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-35-   and click **Connect**. Presets such as Xmind, Notion, and Linear go straight to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:36:   **Connect**. Approve access in the browser window. HTTPS and localhost WebUIs
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-37-   return automatically. From a remote plain-HTTP WebUI, copy the complete
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:38:   localhost callback URL from the browser address bar and paste it into nanobot.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:39:3. Limit the enabled tools when the server exposes more than the task needs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-40-4. Save and restart when prompted.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:41:5. Mention the connected MCP server with `@` in the next message and ask for a small test action.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-42-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-43-For manual or deployment-managed config, add this to `~/.nanobot/config.json`:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-45-```json
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-46-{
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:47:  "tools": {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-48-    "mcpServers": {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-49-      "filesystem": {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-50-        "command": "npx",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:51:        "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/dir"],
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:52:        "enabledTools": ["read_file"]

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-58-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:59:Restart nanobot and ask a question that requires the MCP tool.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-60-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-61-## Production notes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-62-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:63:- Prefer `enabledTools` over exposing every tool by default.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:64:- Use `toolTimeout` for slow MCP operations.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-65-- Use HTTP MCP only for endpoints you trust.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-66-- For deployment-managed OAuth servers, set `auth` to `oauth` and complete the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:67:  browser connection from **Apps → MCP**.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-68-- Keep MCP server commands stable and versioned in deployment docs or scripts.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-69-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-74-  token exchange, and redirects.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-75-- OAuth credentials live in the nanobot data directory, not in `config.json`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:76:- Allow private HTTP MCP hosts only with narrow `tools.ssrfWhitelist` CIDRs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-77-- Do not place secrets in command arguments when environment variables or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-78-  headers can be used.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-81-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-82-- Run the MCP command outside nanobot first.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md:83:- Start `nanobot gateway --verbose` and inspect tool registration logs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-84-- If an HTTP MCP URL is blocked, check whether it points to loopback or a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/configure-mcp-tools.md-85-  private address that needs explicit allowlisting.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-9-| Check | Why it matters |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-10-|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:11:| `nanobot status` shows the expected config and workspace | Confirms the process will read the instance you meant to run |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:12:| `nanobot agent -m "Hello!"` works | Proves install, config, provider, model, and workspace writes before adding a service layer |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-13-| Secrets are in environment variables or protected config files | API keys, bot tokens, OAuth state, and chat credentials should not be world-readable |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:14:| The active config directory (including `sessions/`) and workspace are persistent | Sessions follow `--config`; memory, generated artifacts, and the workspace identity marker follow the workspace |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:15:| Channel access control is intentional | Use `allowFrom`, pairing, WebSocket `token`/`tokenIssueSecret`, or private test channels before exposing the bot |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:16:| Ports are planned | Gateway health defaults to local-only `127.0.0.1:18790`; WebUI/WebSocket defaults to `8765`; `nanobot serve` defaults to `8900` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-17-| Logs are easy to reach | Use `docker compose logs`, `journalctl`, LaunchAgent log files, or `nanobot gateway --verbose` while diagnosing startup |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-18-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-25-| Render | One-click hosted gateway and WebUI | Persistent disk at `/home/nanobot/.nanobot` | [Deploy to Render](#render) |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-26-| Docker Compose | Repeatable container runs on Linux servers or workstations | Bind-mount `~/.nanobot` to `/home/nanobot/.nanobot` | `docker compose run --rm nanobot-cli agent -m "Hello!"` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:27:| Docker CLI | Manual container testing or small one-off hosts | Bind-mount `~/.nanobot` to `/home/nanobot/.nanobot` | `docker run -v ~/.nanobot:/home/nanobot/.nanobot --rm nanobot status` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-28-| systemd user service | Linux user-level gateway that restarts automatically | Host user's `~/.nanobot` unless you pass explicit paths | `systemctl --user status nanobot-gateway` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-29-| macOS LaunchAgent | macOS gateway that starts after login | Host user's `~/.nanobot` unless the plist passes explicit paths | `launchctl list | grep ai.nanobot.gateway` |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-31-## Render
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-32-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:33:Run nanobot online without managing a server. The blueprint deploys the gateway and bundled WebUI together, with a persistent disk so sessions, memory, and chat history survive restarts.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-34-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-35-> [!IMPORTANT]
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-51-### Updates and Data
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-52-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:53:The Blueprint disables automatic deploys so upstream repository changes do not unexpectedly restart your agent. To update, open the service in the Render Dashboard and choose **Manual Deploy → Deploy latest commit**.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-54-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:55:The persistent disk keeps `config.json`, sessions, memory, WebUI history, cron state, media, and logs across restarts and updates. The deployment initializes `config.json` only when it does not already exist, so settings changed later in the WebUI are not replaced on every boot.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-56-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-57-If deployment fails, open the service **Logs** page first. A missing model key fails provider requests after startup, while an incorrect Web token leaves you on the authentication page.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-60-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-61-> [!TIP]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:62:> The `-v ~/.nanobot:/home/nanobot/.nanobot` flag mounts your local config directory into the container, so your config and workspace persist across container restarts.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-63-> The container runs as the non-root user `nanobot` (UID 1000) and reads config from `/home/nanobot/.nanobot`. Always mount your host config directory to `/home/nanobot/.nanobot`, not `/root/.nanobot`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-64-> If you get **Permission denied**, fix ownership on the host first: `sudo chown -R 1000:1000 ~/.nanobot`, or pass `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` to match your host UID. Podman users can use `--userns=keep-id` instead.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-120-handshake and REST requests directly.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-121-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md:122:Set `publicWsUrl` to the browser-facing `wss://` endpoint when the tunnel sends
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-123-the origin host header (such as `127.0.0.1:8765`); otherwise the WebUI could
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-124-attempt to open its WebSocket directly against the loopback address.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-137-a comma-separated `NANOBOT_CHANNELS` build argument:

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-141-```

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-149-is not guaranteed write access to the virtual environment.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/deployment.md-155-```

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/websocket.md-364-## Multi-chat multiplexing
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/websocket.md-365-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/websocket.md:366:A single WebSocket can carry many concurrent chats. The server tracks `chat_id -> {connections}` as a fan-out set, so the same chat can also be mirrored across multiple connections (e.g. two browser tabs).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/websocket.md-367-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-4-@mention or delegated issue. The recommended path uses the nanobot WebUI and a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-5-pre-filled Linear app manifest. Review the generated URLs and subscriptions,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:6:and confirm that webhook delivery is enabled before testing a task.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-7-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-8-> [!NOTE]
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-15-  delegates an issue to it.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-16-- An ordinary issue comment does not invoke nanobot.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:17:- A follow-up inside the existing Agent Session continues the same nanobot
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:18:  session without another @mention.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-19-- Linear's stop control asks nanobot to cancel the active turn. The sender must
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-20-  have access, just as for other requests. An activity already delivered to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-21-  Linear cannot be recalled.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:22:- nanobot reports its acknowledgement, tool activity, reasoning, and final
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-23-  answer as native Linear Agent Activities.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-24-- Button choices are sent as Linear selection activities, and local outbound
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-25-  files are uploaded to Linear before they are linked in the response.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:26:- Private `uploads.linear.app` links in the session prompt are downloaded with
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:27:  the workspace OAuth token and passed to nanobot as inbound media after access
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-28-  checks. A prompt can import up to 10 attachments and 40 MB in total; skipped
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-29-  or unavailable files are called out in the prompt instead of failing silently.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-30-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-31-The OAuth request includes `app:mentionable` and `app:assignable`, in addition
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:32:to `read` and `write`. Existing workspace installations must be reconnected to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-33-grant `app:assignable`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-34-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:35:The native channel owns Agent Session transport. Connect the Linear MCP app when
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:36:the agent also needs tools for searching or changing Linear issues; OAuth scopes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:37:on the channel do not expose those actions as nanobot tools. MCP does not replace
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:38:the channel's OAuth installation, webhook, or Agent Session transport.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-39-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-40-## Before you start
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-41-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:42:There are two separate decisions: **connect a workspace**, then **choose who can
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-43-use nanobot**. The administrator sets up the app once; teammates do not need to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-44-create their own apps, paste credentials, or scan a code.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-46-```text

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-49-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-50-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-54-its members.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-163-### 2. Create the Linear app
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-164-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:165:1. Select **Create Linear app**. Sign in to the Linear workspace in
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-166-   which you want to create the app.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-167-2. Review the pre-filled form. It should describe a **private** app and contain:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-170-   Redirect URI:  https://nanobot.example.com/linear/oauth/callback
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-171-   Webhook URL:   https://nanobot.example.com/linear/webhook
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:172:   Webhook types: AgentSessionEvent, PermissionChange, OAuthAuthorization
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-173-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-174-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-179-   **Disabled**, use the adjacent **…** menu to enable delivery. Confirm the URL
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-180-   points to the current public origin and that **Events** includes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:181:   **Agent session events** (`AgentSessionEvent`).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-182-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-183-> [!IMPORTANT]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-184-> OAuth authorization and webhook delivery are separate. Authorization can
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-185-> succeed while webhook delivery is disabled. In that state, Linear can create
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:186:> an Agent Session, but nanobot receives no task and Linear may report
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-187-> **Agent didn't start** or **nanobot failed to start**.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-188-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-189-Do not add a `Comment` webhook subscription. Linear delivers new @mentions and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md:190:Agent Session follow-ups through `AgentSessionEvent`; subscribing to comments
runtime/cde-20260926/external/nanobot-docs/docs/guides/linear-agent.md-191-would add events that this channel intentionally ignores.
